lines: There's one ticket left. Two users click Buy at the exact same time.
Both check the database. Both see: one ticket available.
Both buy it. Congratulations — you just sold the same ticket twice.
This is called a race condition. Your code worked perfectly… just in the wrong order.
Databases solve this with transactions and locking: one operation finishes before the other can change the same data.
If two things can happen at the same time, assume someday they will.
